reading.title: Show, Don't Tell: Describing a Character
reading.purpose: See how writers show what a character is like through the way the character acts.
paras: Writers want you to know a character well, but they do not always say what the character is like. Instead, they show it. If you read the actions closely, you can name the trait yourself.

Look at how a character behaves around other people. A timid character hides behind a door or whispers an answer. A bashful character blushes and stares at the floor when someone says hello. A boastful character brags about winning, even when nobody asked. A courteous character, which means a polite and respectful one, says please and thank you and holds the door for others.

Some characters bring trouble into a story. A mischievous character hides a friend's pencil just for fun. A sly character grins and keeps a secret plan to himself, because he is clever in a tricky way. A clumsy character trips over a chair or drops a whole tray of lunches. An obedient character, on the other hand, does exactly what the coach or the teacher asks.

Moods and places matter too. A cranky character snaps at friends because she slept badly and feels annoyed. On a gloomy day, with dark clouds and cold rain, even a happy scene can feel sad. When a writer picks these details with care, readers feel that they know the person.
The next time you read, pause and ask what the character's actions show. Then choose just the right word to describe that person.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, the word "sly" most nearly means
choices: slow and careful with every step
playful in a loud and silly way
clever in a tricky, secret way
unwilling to share a plan with anyone
qs.why: The sentence explains it: the character is "clever in a tricky way" and keeps a secret plan.

qs.q: Which sentence tells how a bashful character acts?
choices: A timid character hides behind a door or whispers an answer.
A boastful character brags about winning, even when nobody asked.
A courteous character, which means a polite and respectful one, says please and thank you and holds the door for others.
A bashful character blushes and stares at the floor when someone says hello.
qs.why: This is the only sentence about a bashful character, and it shows blushing and looking down when greeted.

ev.text: A bashful character blushes and stares at the floor when someone says hello.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Characters in most stories are shy or cranky, and writers must say so.
Writers show a character's traits through actions, moods, and details.
Trouble makes a story more exciting than a calm story ever could.
A gloomy day, with dark clouds, is the best way to start a story.
qs.why: Each paragraph gives examples of actions and details that show a trait, and the last one tells readers to use them.

qs.q: A girl says, "I am the best singer in the whole school," three times before lunch. Which word from the reading fits her?
qs.why: The reading says a boastful character brags about winning, which is like praising yourself again and again.
